question.text: A certain elastic conducting material is stretched into a circular loop. It is placed with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. When released the radius of the loop starts shrinking at a constant rate of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The induced emf in the loop at an instant when the radius of the loop is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mV</mi></math>.

solution.text:
According to the Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the emf induced in a conducting loop is given by, e=-dϕdt, here, t is time and ϕ=BA is magnetic flux.

Here, e=dϕdt=dBAdt=Bdπr2dt

=Bπ2rdrdt=2×π×0.1×0.8×2×10-2

 ≈10 mV (rounded off)
